## Natural history notes

A freshwater mussel characterized by its elongated, dark brown to black shell and slightly compressed, oval shape. In Florida, it is found in rivers, streams, and other freshwater systems, often in sandy or muddy substrates. Like other native freshwater mussels, it is a filter feeder that helps improve water quality and depends on fish hosts during its larval life stage.
